program_name: ENGLISH CURRICULUM NAME: 'Mechanical Engineering for Design and Manufacturing - Curriculum in Sustainable Development'. ITALIAN DIPLOMA NAME (what the degree certificate actually says): 'Ingegneria Meccanica per la Progettazione e la Produzione'. This item is NOT a standalone English-taught degree. It is one curriculum inside an Italian-registered Laurea Magistrale, and the qualification awarded is the Italian degree in Ingegneria Meccanica per la Progettazione e la Produzione (class LM-33) regardless of which curriculum the student followed. The curriculum is not a separate degree title and, on the evidence found, is not itself named on the diploma (see uncertainty_notes). OFFICIAL ENGLISH NAME OF THE PARENT DEGREE: the Didactic Regulations cover sheet reads 'DIDACTIC REGULATIONS OF THE DEGREE PROGRAM - MECHANICAL ENGINEERING FOR DESIGN AND MANUFACTURING - CLASS LM-33', and the University's own International course catalogue lists it as 'Mechanical Engineering for Design and Manufacturing'. NAME INCONSISTENCY ON UNINA.IT ITSELF: the Department of Industrial Engineering programme site uses BOTH English renderings - 'Master's Degree in Mechanical Engineering for Design and Manufacturing' on its General Information page and in the brochure, but 'Master's Degree Mechanical Engineering for Design and Production' in its own site navigation and on the orientation page ('The Master's Degree Programme in Mechanical Engineering for Design and Production (LM-IMPP)'). 'Manufacturing' and 'Production' are the same degree; 'Production' is a literal rendering of the Italian 'Produzione'. Use 'Manufacturing' - that is the form in the Didactic Regulations and in the International course catalogue. PROGRAMME ACRONYM used internally: LM-IMPP (or IMPP). OFFICIAL COURSE CODE at Federico II: D19 - stated on the programme's own contacts page: 'This page lists the main contacts for the Master's Degree in Mechanical Engineering for Design and Manufacturing (D19)'. Course catalogue sheets therefore sit under www.corsi.unina.it/D19 (e.g. www.corsi.unina.it/D19/insegnamenti/... for individual course sheets). MINISTERIAL SUA IDENTIFIER: 'SUA ID=1604844' (Didactic Regulations Art. 1). STRUCTURE: Laurea Magistrale (2-year Master of Science), 2 years, 120 CFU/ECTS, maximum 12 examinations including the final exam. School: Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base (Polytechnic and Basic Sciences). Department: Dipartimento di Ingegneria Industriale (DII). Programme Coordinator: Prof. Enrico Armentani (enrico.armentani@unina.it, +39 081 768 2450). CURRICULUM COUNT - CORRECTION TO THE RESEARCH BRIEF: the brief states the programme has 5 curricula of which only 'Sustainable Development' is in English. The 2026/2027 official sources say THREE curricula, and it is the FIRST curriculum that is subdivided into five tracks. Didactic Regulations Art. 2: 'The training path includes three curricula, one of which is taught entirely in English.' Programme Catalogue: 'The study programme offers three curricula, one of which is delivered entirely in English.' The three are: (1) the Generalist curriculum, subdivided into five tracks - Advanced and Smart Mechanical Design, Advanced and Smart Production (a.k.a. Advanced and Smart Manufacturing), Road Vehicle Design (called simply 'Vehicle Design' in the Didactic Regulations), Technological Processes (called 'Manufacturing Processes' on the orientation page), Mechatronics; (2) Railway Mechanics; (3) Sustainable Development, in English. The brochure phrases the same thing as 'one of the 5 paths or 2 curricula'. So the '5' in the brief is the number of TRACKS in the generalist curriculum, not the number of curricula. OPTIONAL ADD-ON: students may take the 'Minor in Applied Machine Learning' (27 CFU, of which at least 6 extra-curricular, giving 126 total CFU), governed by separate University regulations and giving rise to a career distinct from the degree.
level: master - Laurea Magistrale (2-year second-cycle Master of Science, 120 CFU/ECTS), class LM-33 Mechanical Engineering. Not a single-cycle degree and not a first-level/second-level 'Master' in the Italian professional sense. orientamento.unina.it classifies it under 'Master's Degree'; the University's International course catalogue lists it under '2-year Master's degrees (LM) > Engineering'.
teaching_language: PROGRAMME LEVEL: Italian AND English. orientamento.unina.it lists 'Language ENG/ITA' on the English course profile and 'Lingua ITA/ENG' on the Italian one. The University's International course catalogue lists the entry as 'Mechanical Engineering for Design and Manufacturing ITA/ENG' (contrast the fully English degrees in the same list, marked '- ENG', e.g. Autonomous Vehicle Engineering, Data Science, Transportation Engineering and Mobility). Didactic Regulations Art. 1: the degree 'is offered in both Italian and English'. CURRICULUM LEVEL - THIS IS THE POINT OF THE ITEM: of the three curricula, ONLY 'Sustainable Development' is taught in English; the Generalist curriculum (five tracks) and the Railway Mechanics curriculum are taught in ITALIAN. Didactic Regulations Art. 2: 'The training path includes three curricula, one of which is taught entirely in English' and 'The third curriculum, in Sustainable Development, is taught in English.' Programme Catalogue A.Y. 2026-2027: 'The study programme offers three curricula, one of which is delivered entirely in English. ... The third curriculum, in Sustainable Development, is taught in English and aims at the design and realisation of industrial products that meet new or evolving user needs.' The orientamento.unina.it study-plan section heads the block 'The Curriculum in Sustainable Development (in English)'. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR AN INTERNATIONAL APPLICANT: an applicant who does not speak Italian must commit to the Sustainable Development curriculum specifically, and must say so in writing. Study Plan annex, note a) to the Sustainable Development table: 'A student who wishes to follow the Sustainable Development Curriculum must notify this in writing at the time of enrollment.' Choosing any other curriculum, or drifting into Italian-taught electives from Tables G1/G2/G3, puts the student into Italian-taught classes. WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN ENGLISH INSIDE THE CURRICULUM: the Sustainable Development first-year mandatory pool (36 CFU chosen from Advanced Structural Mechanics, Mechanical vibrations, Logistics and Operation Management, Digital Modeling and Simulation for Industrial Engineering, Advanced and Resource Efficient Manufacturing) and the curricular/affine tables published for it (Table G1: Applied Mechanics for Energy Efficiency, Modeling and Experimentation for Smart Vehicles, AI aided Structural Design, Bio-Inspired Generative Design for Additive Manufacturing, Design of Mechatronic Systems, Design Methods for Sustainable Products, Additive Manufacturing, Green Manufacturing and Sustainability, Sustainable Manufacturing Technologies, Smart Production Systems, Smart Modelling of Industrial Production Systems; Table G2: Advanced and Sustainable Materials Selection, Statistical Learning for Industrial Engineering, Machine Learning for Engineering, Sustainable Metallurgy). Note that some of these titles also appear, in Italian, in the generalist tracks (e.g. 'Advanced and Resource Efficient Manufacturing' = 'Tecnologie Speciali'; 'Mechanical Vibrations' = 'Dinamica dei Sistemi Meccanici'; 'Logistics and Operation Management' = 'Gestione della Produzione Industriale'; 'Digital Modeling and Simulation for Industrial Engineering' = 'Modellazione Geometrica e Prototipazione Virtuale'), i.e. the same subject is delivered in Italian in the generalist tracks and in English in the Sustainable Development curriculum. [uncertain] I did not find a per-course language field published on unina.it confirming, course sheet by course sheet, that every Sustainable Development course is delivered in English; the English-medium claim rests on the Didactic Regulations, the Programme Catalogue and the orientamento profile, which state it directly for the curriculum as a whole. THESIS AND FINAL EXAM: may be in English regardless of curriculum - orientamento.unina.it: 'The written thesis and the defense may be presented in English.' NOTE ON ITALIAN: no Italian-language teaching requirement is imposed by the programme for the Sustainable Development curriculum, but the programme is administratively an Italian/English degree, and much of the department's own web material, the study-plan tables, the didactic calendar and the student secretariat operate in Italian. See language_requirements for the university-level Italian B2 question, which is genuinely unresolved for this programme.

degree_class: LM-33 - Ingegneria Meccanica / Mechanical Engineering. Stated on the Didactic Regulations cover ('CLASS LM-33'), on the orientamento.unina.it profile ('Degree class LM-33'), on the programme's General Information page ('Master's Degree Class: LM-33 - Mechanical Engineering') and on the department's access-requirements text ('access to the Master's Degree Programme in Mechanical Engineering for Design and Production (LM-33)'). The Sustainable Development curriculum does not have its own degree class - it is LM-33 like the rest of the programme. AlmaLaurea records the same programme under codicione 0630107303400001 (LM-33).
admission_type: OPEN ACCESS (accesso libero / non a numero programmato), CONDITIONAL ON TWO CHECKS. There is no ranking, no competitive selection, no bando/call and no quota. What there is: (1) verification of CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (a documentary check of the applicant's bachelor transcript against a list of minimum CFU per scientific-disciplinary sector), and (2) verification of the ADEQUACY OF PERSONAL PREPARATION, which is automatic if the bachelor weighted average is at least 24/30 and otherwise requires passing a multiple-choice admission test. Language competence is checked as part of (2). orientamento.unina.it summarises the access mode in one line: English profile 'Admission: Verifica di preparazione'; Italian profile 'Accesso: Verifica di preparazione'; entry qualification 'Degree required: Laurea I Livello' / 'Titolo di ingresso: Laurea I Livello'. orientamento.unina.it, Admission and prerequisites: 'Access to the Master's Degree Program in Mechanical Engineering for Design and Manufacturing is open, subject to verification of the possession of the curricular requirements specified in the Program's Teaching Regulations, as well as verification of the adequacy of the student's personal preparation.' CONFIRMED NOT RESTRICTED-ACCESS: the University's official 'Corsi a numero programmato' page for a.y. 2026/2027 does not list this programme, nor any LM-33 or any engineering Laurea Magistrale. The only engineering entry in that list is the single-cycle Ingegneria Edile-Architettura; the restricted-access Lauree Magistrali are Precision Livestock Farming, Professioni sanitarie, Psicologia Clinica e degli interventi nei contesti sociali e dello sviluppo, Scienze Enologiche and Scienze della Nutrizione Umana. The Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base states the same rule generally: 'L'ammissione ai Corsi di Laurea Magistrale non a ciclo unico prevede, ai sensi del DM 270/04, la verifica del possesso dei requisiti curriculari nonche' la verifica della personale preparazione dello studente.' The PAN/PAL/TA-OFA/TOLC admission machinery described on that page applies to BACHELOR degrees, not to this master's - there is NO TOLC and NO SAT for this programme. CURRICULUM CHOICE IS NOT A SELECTION. Entering the Sustainable Development curriculum is not competitive and has no separate quota; it is a declaration. Study Plan annex, note a): 'A student who wishes to follow the Sustainable Development Curriculum must notify this in writing at the time of enrollment.' The programme's Study Plans page adds: 'For newly enrolled students, the selection of an Automatically Approved Study Plan takes place directly during enrolment on Segrepass.' IF THE CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS ARE NOT MET, enrolment is refused until they are made up. Didactic Regulations Art. 5.3: 'Enrollment in the Master's Degree in Mechanical Engineering for Design and Manufacturing is not allowed if the minimum curricular requirements are not met. If the minimum requirements are not satisfied, the CCD assists the student by prescribing enrollment in individual courses offered by the University and passing the relevant exams before registration.' The department's access text lists three remedies the CCD may choose between: (a) integrations completed BEFORE enrolment via single course units (corsi singoli), (b) enrolment in a bachelor's degree that gives automatic access, with an abbreviated path, or (c) enrolment in the master's with an individual study plan containing an alignment path 'without any increase in the total number of CFU credits required'. FOR NON-EU APPLICANTS RESIDING ABROAD an additional national procedure sits on top: compulsory pre-enrolment on the Universitaly portal, then a study visa. That is a visa procedure, not a selection - see application_deadline_non_eu.
academic_requirements:
ENTRY QUALIFICATION. A Laurea (Italian three-year bachelor, including pre-DM 509/1999 degrees), or a three-year university diploma, or a foreign qualification recognised as equivalent. Didactic Regulations Art. 4: 'To enroll in a Master's Degree Course, a student must hold a Bachelor's Degree or a three-year university diploma, or another qualification obtained abroad and recognized as valid. Specific curricular requirements and a mandatory verification of the student's personal preparation are also required. This includes the possession of adequate language skills.' orientamento.unina.it lists the entry title as 'Laurea I Livello'. 

CURRICULAR REQUIREMENT - ROUTE 1 (automatic): hold a bachelor's degree in the Italian class L-9 Industrial Engineering (or Class 10 of DM 509/99), or an equivalent qualification. 

CURRICULAR REQUIREMENT - ROUTE 2 (the route almost every foreign applicant takes): show AT LEAST 90 CFU/ECTS distributed across prescribed scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD), in three nested blocks. 
(A) AT LEAST 40 CFU in basic-science sectors: MATH-02/A Algebra; MATH-02/B Geometry; MATH-03/A Mathematical Analysis; MATH-03/B Probability and Mathematical Statistics; MATH-04/A Mathematical Physics; MATH-05/A Numerical Analysis; MATH-06/A Operations Research; STAT-01/A Statistics; STAT-01/B Statistics for Experimental and Technological Research; IINF-05/A Information Processing Systems; PHYS-01/A Experimental physics of fundamental interactions and applications; PHYS-03/A Experimental physics of matter and applications; PHYS-04/A Theoretical physics of matter; CHEM-03/A General and Inorganic Chemistry; CHEM-04/A Science and Technology of Polymeric Materials; CHEM-06/A Principles of Chemistry for Applied Technologies. (These are the new-code SSDs; the department's orientation page prints the same list with the pre-reform equivalents, e.g. MATH-03/A = ex MAT/05, PHYS-01/A = ex FIS/01, CHEM-03/A = ex CHIM/03, and shows CHEM-04/A as 'ex CHIM/05 - Industrial Chemistry' and CHEM-06/A as 'ex CHIM/07'.) 
(B) AT LEAST 50 CFU in engineering sectors: CEAR-06/A Structural Mechanics (ex ICAR/08); IIND-01/D Aerospace Structures and Constructions (ex ING-IND/04); IIND-01/F Fluid dynamics; IIND-01/G Aerospace propulsion; IIND-06/A Fluid Machinery (ex ING-IND/08); IIND-06/B Energy Systems and Power Generation (ex ING-IND/09); IIND-07/A Thermal Engineering and Industrial Energy Systems (ex ING-IND/10); IIND-07/B Building Physics and Building Energy Systems (ex ING-IND/11); IMIS-01/A Mechanical and Thermal Measurements (ex ING-IND/12); IIND-02/A Applied Mechanics (ex ING-IND/13); IIND-03/A Mechanical Design and Machine Construction (ex ING-IND/14); IIND-03/B Design Methods for Industrial Engineering (ex ING-IND/15); IIND-04/A Manufacturing Technology and Systems (ex ING-IND/16); IIND-05/A Industrial Mechanical Systems Engineering (ex ING-IND/17); IIND-03/C Metallurgy (ex ING-IND/21); IMAT-01/A Materials Science and Technology (ex ING-IND/22); IIET-01/A Electrical Engineering (ex ING-IND/31); IIND-08/A Power Electronic Converters, Electrical Machines and Drives (ex ING-IND/32); IEGE-01/A Business and Management Engineering (ex ING-IND/35). Note the three aerospace/fluid sectors IIND-01/F, IIND-01/G and PHYS-04/A appear in the 2026/2027 Didactic Regulations list but not in the department's older orientation-page rendering - the Regulations are the newer text. 
(C) OF THOSE 50, AT LEAST 24 CFU must be in the five CORE MECHANICAL sectors: IIND-02/A Applied Mechanics, IIND-03/A Mechanical Design and Machine Construction, IIND-03/B Design Methods for Industrial Engineering, IIND-04/A Manufacturing Technology and Systems, IIND-05/A Industrial Mechanical Systems Engineering. THIS 24-CFU CORE IS THE USUAL STICKING POINT FOR FOREIGN APPLICANTS. 

EQUIVALENCE AND SHORTFALL. Didactic Regulations Art. 5.3: 'With reference to the requirement of having at least 24 CFU in the sectors IIND-02/A, IIND-03/A, IIND-03/B, IIND-04/A, IIND-05/A, the CCD may identify equivalencies for credits earned in different scientific-disciplinary sectors, based on the content of specific courses from the student's previous academic career, provided these are closely related to the topics of the aforementioned sectors. Students holding an L-9 degree or equivalent but with fewer than 24 CFU in the sectors ... will be admitted to the Master's Degree program with the recommendation of an Individual Study Plan that includes a specific alignment path, without an increase in the total number of CFU.' The department's access text adds that the listed CFU thresholds 'are necessary but not sufficient for enrolment' and that the CCD 'will assess the possession of the cultural requirements deemed necessary ... by analysing the student's curriculum in detail'. So the transcript is read course by course, not just totalled. 

PERSONAL-PREPARATION REQUIREMENT. Didactic Regulations Art. 5: 'the weighted average (M) is calculated based on the CFU and the grades (in thirtieths) obtained in the exams required to earn the degree that grants access to the Master's Degree program. A student's personal preparation is considered adequate if M >= 24. Students who do not meet the weighted average requirement (M) will have to take a specific admission test.' The department states the same as: 'Students whose average mark (out of 30) achieved in the examinations passed for the Bachelor's Degree granting access to the Master's Degree Programme is not lower than 24 are exempted from this verification.' [uncertain] No published rule explains how a foreign grading scale is converted to the Italian /30 scale for the M >= 24 test; in practice this is decided by the CCD when it reads the transcript. 

LANGUAGE IS PART OF THE ACADEMIC CHECK, at B1 - see language_requirements. 

NOTHING CURRICULUM-SPECIFIC. There is no additional or different academic requirement for the Sustainable Development curriculum: the entry gate is the same LM-33 gate, and the curriculum is chosen afterwards by written notification at enrolment. No GRE/GMAT, no portfolio, no research proposal, no minimum work experience, no reference letters are required by any published unina.it rule for this programme.
entry_exam_or_test:
THERE IS AN ADMISSION TEST, BUT MOST APPLICANTS NEVER SIT IT. It is triggered only when the applicant's bachelor weighted average is below 24/30 (see academic_requirements). It is a threshold test, not a competitive one - there is no ranking and no quota, you either clear the bar or you retake. 
FORMAT (department's published access rules, per the Teaching Coordination Committee resolution of 23 July 2024): 'The admission test consists of a questionnaire made up of 35 multiple-choice questions, randomly drawn from a pool of 140. In particular, in order to provide balanced coverage of the seven characterising subject areas of Mechanical Engineering (IIND-06/A ex ING-IND/08, IIND-07/A ex ING-IND/10, IIND-02/A ex ING-IND/13, IIND-03/A ex ING-IND/14, IIND-03/B ex ING-IND/15, IIND-04/A ex ING-IND/16, IIND-05/A ex ING-IND/17), 5 questions are randomly selected from 20 available for each subject area. The test is considered passed if the student answers correctly at least 21 of the 35 questions.' 
PASS MARK: 21/35 (60%). SEVEN SUBJECT AREAS x 5 QUESTIONS: fluid machinery, industrial thermal engineering, applied mechanics, mechanical design and machine construction, industrial engineering drawing/design methods, manufacturing technologies and systems, mechanical industrial plants. 
THE ENTIRE QUESTION BANK IS PUBLISHED IN ADVANCE: 'The full set of 140 questions is available at the following link: http://meccanica.dii.unina.it/images/lmpp/Lista_domande_Test.pdf'. The department frames this as a self-assessment tool as well: 'the 140 questions are specifically designed to evaluate the individual knowledge in the core subject areas of Mechanical Engineering. These questions offer a valuable opportunity to independently assess one's level of preparation and to identify any gaps.' 
ATTEMPTS: 'The test may be taken a maximum of three times, with a minimum interval of one month between two consecutive attempts.' And: 'should a student fail the test on one of the dates listed above, they will not be permitted to take the test on the immediately following date.' 
YOU MAY SIT IT BEFORE GRADUATING: 'Each student may take the test even before obtaining their Bachelor's Degree, in order to assess their preparation in view of future enrolment in the Master's Degree Programme.' 
SCHEDULED SESSIONS PUBLISHED BY THE PROGRAMME, valid for BOTH mechanical master's degrees ('In compliance with the Programme Regulations for access to the Master's Degree Programmes in Mechanical Engineering for Energy and Environment and Mechanical Engineering for Design and Production, the schedule for the assessment test, set up to December 2026, is provided below'): 2026-01-20, 2026-02-24, 2026-04-07, 2026-06-22, 2026-07-21, 2026-10-13, 2026-11-10, 2026-12-22. 
BOOKING: a Microsoft Forms registration form linked from the programme orientation page (forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=auLPL2K7sEax4yj52gxF_SXeNKE0iP1Iolr3mbJyvztUMDZRWDFIQVRHSzVMQVdQVEJWUUdHMVAxQy4u). 
EXAMINING COMMITTEE for the sessions listed above: President Prof. Luca Esposito; Commissioners Ing. Luca Boccarusso and Ing. Luca Viscito. 
DISCRETIONARY ALTERNATIVES. The department's rules do not make the 35-question test the only possible route: 'Applications for admission to the Master's Degree Programme by students who do not meet the criteria for automatic admission will be examined by the CCD, which will assess at its sole discretion the admissibility of the application ... The CCD may examine the candidate's academic record, where appropriate taking into account the marks obtained in characterising courses ... or by setting up assessment procedures (interviews, tests) to verify the adequacy of the student's individual academic preparation, or by adopting procedures 1 or 3 envisaged for the curricular integrations.' So an interview is possible in place of the written test, at the CCD's discretion. 
SEPARATE LANGUAGE TEST. A student who holds neither a degree taught in Italian or English nor a B1 Italian/English certificate must additionally 'demonstrate adequate comprehension and conversation skills in either Italian or English through a proficiency test' (Didactic Regulations Art. 5). This is distinct from the 35-question subject test. 
NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO GRE/GMAT, NO NATIONAL TEST. TOLC applies only to Federico II bachelor programmes in Engineering and Sciences. 
[uncertain] The published test calendar, the booking form and the question-bank PDF are on the department's site in a page that mixes Italian and English and does not state whether the test paper itself is available in English, nor whether it can be sat remotely from abroad. The dates listed run only 'up to December 2026'; 2027 dates were not published at the research date.
seats_total: NO SEAT CAP - the programme is open access. No number of places is published anywhere on unina.it for this degree, because none exists: the University's official 'Corsi a numero programmato' list for a.y. 2026/2027 does not include this programme or any engineering Laurea Magistrale, and the orientamento.unina.it profile states access is 'open, subject to verification of the possession of the curricular requirements ... as well as verification of the adequacy of the student's personal preparation'. Anyone who clears the curricular and personal-preparation checks may enrol. Consequently there is no ranking list (graduatoria) and no bando fixing places. NO CAP ON THE CURRICULUM EITHER: the Sustainable Development curriculum has no published maximum number of students; entry to it is by written notification at enrolment, not by allocation. [uncertain] Class-size limits could in principle be applied administratively (e.g. laboratory capacity), but nothing of the kind is published for this programme.
non_eu_reserved_seats: NONE - no seats are reserved for, or capped for, non-EU applicants. Reserved non-EU quotas at Federico II exist only for restricted-access (numero programmato) programmes, and this programme is not one of them (verified against the University's 'Corsi a numero programmato' 2026/2027 list, which contains no LM-33 and no engineering Laurea Magistrale). Non-EU applicants residing abroad still have to go through the compulsory Universitaly pre-enrolment and study-visa procedure, but that is a visa pipeline with a hard DATE (15 June 2026), not a NUMBER of places - see application_deadline_non_eu. Non-EU applicants who are already legally resident in Italy or in an EU country are treated exactly like EU applicants: international.unina.it, 'Non-European candidates, wherever they reside and regularly residing in Italy or in a European Union country, have unrestricted access to university courses if they hold a qualification corresponding to the required Italian qualification ... You will therefore not need to pre-register on the Universitaly Portal.'
language_requirements:
[uncertain] THREE SEPARATE LANGUAGE RULES OPERATE AT THREE LEVELS AND THEY ARE NOT ALIGNED. Read all three; the third is the one that can actually derail a non-EU applicant to this particular degree. 

RULE 1 - PROGRAMME LEVEL, FOR ADMISSION: B1 in ITALIAN **OR** ENGLISH, and only if you cannot show a degree taught in one of those languages. This is only B1, not B2, and Italian is an accepted alternative to English. Didactic Regulations Art. 5, verbatim: 'Regarding the verification of language skills, students who do not hold a qualification obtained by attending a study program delivered in Italian or English, and who do not have certifications or language qualifications attesting to their knowledge of Italian or English at least at level B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR), must demonstrate adequate comprehension and conversation skills in either Italian or English through a proficiency test.' Practical effect: a bachelor's degree delivered in English satisfies the programme's own admission language rule outright, with no certificate at all. 

RULE 2 - PROGRAMME LEVEL, FOR GRADUATION: B2 in an EU language other than Italian - in practice English - carried as 3 CFU of 'Additional Language Skills'. This is NOT an entry barrier; it is a graduation requirement you can satisfy during the degree. Didactic Regulations Art. 5: 'since to obtain the Master's Degree the student must be able to use a European Union language fluently, in addition to Italian, the study plan includes a sufficient number of CFU (at least 3) to acquire Additional language knowledge, particularly in English. The attainment of this knowledge, at least at level B2, will be certified in accordance with the methods defined by the University's Language Center (www.cla.unina.it). Students already in possession of an English certificate at least at the B2 level upon registration may request its recognition.' The Study Plan annex repeats it as note c) on the Sustainable Development table and the orientamento study-plan listing shows it as first-year item d) 'foreign language proficiency (e.g., English B2 level certification or equivalent), 3 CFU'. 
TWO ROUTES, from the programme's 'Additional Knowledge' page: (a) 'Students who already hold a B2 (CEFR) English certificate issued by a certified centre external to the University may request the recognition of 3 ECTS of additional language skills by emailing the certificate to the Programme office'; (b) 'Students who do not already hold such a certificate may obtain it by taking the B2 Placement Test organised by the University Language Centre (CLA) ... The test schedule is published at https://www.cla.unina.it/placement_test. Following the test, the CLA will notify the Programme Coordinator of the result for the recognition of the 3 ECTS ... Students who do not pass the Placement Test may follow an online B2 remedial course organised by the CLA (https://www.cla.unina.it/bacheca) and subsequently retake the test.' The 3 CFU are pass/fail: 'These 3 ECTS are awarded with a pass/fail outcome (no grade), only an eligibility.' No closed list of accepted certificate providers and no recency limit is published for this programme. 

RULE 3 - UNIVERSITY / MINISTRY LEVEL, FOR NON-EU PRE-ENROLMENT: B2 ITALIAN, for programmes taught in Italian. THIS IS THE UNRESOLVED POINT FOR THIS DEGREE. international.unina.it, verbatim: '1. If you choose a three-year degree course, magistral degree course or single-cycle magistral degree course in ITALIAN, a B2 level Italian language proficiency is required', proven either by uploading to Universitaly a CLIQ-system certificate (Universita per Stranieri di Perugia or Siena, Roma Tre, Societa Dante Alighieri, or the Universita per Stranieri Dante Alighieri di Reggio Calabria, including via Italian Cultural Institutes abroad) or by sitting an Italian proficiency test whose 'procedures and timing will be communicated by e-mail by the coordinator of the chosen course'. And: '2. If you choose a three-year, five-year or single-cycle degree course in ENGLISH, level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required. Remember that an international certificate attesting to the level of English language skills (IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge, etc.) is useful for the issue of the visa.' 
WHY THIS IS AMBIGUOUS HERE: the University registers this degree as ITA/ENG, not ENG. In the International course catalogue it appears as 'Mechanical Engineering for Design and Manufacturing ITA/ENG', unlike the fully English degrees marked '- ENG'. The English exemption in Rule 3 is written for a course 'in ENGLISH'. A candidate who selects this degree on Universitaly is selecting the LM-33 degree, not the curriculum - Universitaly has no field for a curriculum. So it is genuinely unclear whether the Italian B2 requirement is waived for someone who intends to follow the Sustainable Development curriculum. Note also that the sentence exempting English-taught courses lists 'three-year, five-year or single-cycle' and omits the two-year magistrale, whereas the sentence imposing Italian B2 explicitly includes 'magistral degree course' - a drafting asymmetry on unina.it's own page that cuts against the applicant. TREAT ITALIAN B2 AS A LIVE RISK AND SETTLE IT IN WRITING WITH THE PROGRAMME COORDINATOR (enrico.armentani@unina.it) AND THE ENGINEERING INTERNATIONAL DESK (antonietta.telese@unina.it, francesca.candida@unina.it) BEFORE FILING ON UNIVERSITALY. 

WHAT THE SISTER PROGRAMME DOES (evidence of departmental practice, NOT a published rule for this degree). The same Department of Industrial Engineering publishes an international-admissions FAQ for the OTHER mechanical master's, Mechanical Engineering for Energy and Environment (LM-IMEA), whose English-taught curriculum is 'Sustainable Energy'. It requires: 'Proof of English language proficiency at minimum B2 level (CEFR), such as IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge English (B2 First, C1 Advanced, etc.), Pearson PTE Academic, or equivalent internationally recognized certificates' with the alternative 'instead of a language certificate, applicants may submit an official statement certifying that the entire degree program was fully taught in English (Medium of Instruction, MOI)'. It also says 'For international students, the Sustainable Energy curriculum, entirely taught in English, is strongly recommended.' NO EQUIVALENT FAQ IS PUBLISHED FOR THIS DEGREE (LM-IMPP). The FAQ index on the department site carries only a '- LM-IMEA -' block. Expect the coordinator to apply something similar in practice, but do not treat English B2 + MOI as a documented rule for LM-IMPP. 

BOTTOM LINE FOR AN INTERNATIONAL APPLICANT: bring an English B2 (IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge/PTE) or an MOI statement - it satisfies Rule 1 at admission, pre-clears the 3 CFU of Rule 2, and supports the visa application. Do not assume you are exempt from Italian B2 under Rule 3 until the coordinator confirms it in writing.

What binds instead are (A) the admission-evaluation step, which has no fixed date but should be started early, (B) the University's enrolment calendar, and (C) the study-plan / curriculum-declaration deadline. All dates below are the University's official a.y. 2026/2027 dates from the binding 'Guida all'iscrizione Anno accademico 2026-27', the document the programme's own orientamento page points to under 'Application timeline'. 

(A) ADMISSION EVALUATION - NO DEADLINE, DO IT EARLY. Holders of an Italian qualification apply through the School's graduate-admission procedure and are assessed by the CCD. Holders of a FOREIGN qualification who are EU citizens - or non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy or the EU - must, per international.unina.it, 'send your academic documents to the Coordinator of the course you wish to enrol in to find out whether you meet the enrolment requirements'; for this degree the Coordinator is Prof. Enrico Armentani (enrico.armentani@unina.it). If the bachelor average is under 24/30, the 35-question admission test must be scheduled - the published 2026 sessions are 20 Jan, 24 Feb, 07 Apr, 22 Jun, 21 Jul, 13 Oct, 10 Nov and 22 Dec, with a minimum one-month gap between attempts and no retake on the immediately following date after a fail. If the curricular requirements fall short, the CCD may require credits to be earned via single course units BEFORE enrolment, which can cost a semester or more. Start months ahead of the enrolment window.

CRITICAL WARNING PUBLISHED BY THE UNIVERSITY: 'Be aware that pre-enrolment alone does not grant admission to degree programmes. In order to matriculate you also need to take and pass the verifications of the entry requirements and the admission procedures set for the degree programme of your interest.' And: 'Important! The University of Naples Federico II does not issue admission letters for obtaining a visa.' NON-EU APPLICANTS ALREADY LEGALLY RESIDENT IN ITALY OR THE EU ARE NOT ON THIS TIMETABLE: 'Non-European candidates, wherever they reside and regularly residing in Italy or in a European Union country, have unrestricted access to university courses if they hold a qualification corresponding to the required Italian qualification ... you may present your academic documents directly to the Coordinator of the Course in which you wish to enrol. THERE IS NO SINGLE PUBLISHED CHECKLIST FOR THIS PROGRAMME. Four different lists apply depending on who you are and which stage you are at. 

(1) FOR THE ACADEMIC EVALUATION BY THE PROGRAMME COORDINATOR / CCD (every applicant with a foreign qualification, EU or non-EU). international.unina.it requires you to 'send your academic documents to the Coordinator of the course you wish to enrol in' and to 'produce any documentation that the University deems necessary for the evaluation of the foreign qualification': 
- eventual translations 
- legalisations 
- Diploma Supplement 
- certificates of examinations (transcript of records) 
- certificates from the Italian ENIC-NARIC centre (CIMEA), https://www.cimea.it/EN/ 
- any declarations of value (dichiarazione di valore) issued by the competent diplomatic representations. 
Because the curricular check is CFU-by-SSD (see academic_requirements), the transcript must show credit values and, ideally, syllabi, so the CCD can map your courses onto IIND-02/A, IIND-03/A, IIND-03/B, IIND-04/A and IIND-05/A. 

(2) FOR NON-EU PRE-ENROLMENT / THE VISA (Universitaly + Embassy). international.unina.it, 'You must take the following documents to the Italian Embassy': 'the summary of the pre-enrolment application submitted through Universitaly and validated by the University of Naples Federico II; any language competence certificates (see information on how to meet the Italian language requirement); the documents required for the visa application, including a health insurance policy where applicable; the required documents if you hold a foreign qualification.' Plus the visa-requirement evidence: proof of EUR 10,179.85/year subsistence, repatriation funds or return ticket, accommodation in Italy, and medical/hospitalisation insurance valid in Italy without limits on emergency hospitalisation. 

(3) FOR ENROLMENT (matriculation) - international.unina.it, 'Documents required for enrolment': 
- Copy of passport 
- Application form 
- 1 passport photo 
- Tax code (codice fiscale) 
- Residence permit (or proof of having applied for it) 
- 'Declaration of value issued by the Italian Embassy in the country where the degree was obtained or certificate of validity issued by ENIC-NARIC centres.' The page adds: 'Important: always check the instructions on the degree programme's website.' Non-EU students complete enrolment through the competent Secretary's office (Ufficio Area Didattica Ingegneria, Piazzale Tecchio 80) rather than purely online. Italian/EU students enrol through SegrePass (www.segrepass.unina.it). 

(4) PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC ITEMS: 
- WRITTEN NOTIFICATION OF THE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT CURRICULUM, at enrolment (Study Plan annex note a). Without it you are not in the English curriculum.

No such list, form or letter procedure is published for LM-IMPP. Treat the LM-IMEA list as a realistic preview of what the department will ask for, not as a rule for this degree - and confirm with the coordinator.

The programme's own website publishes NO fee page. 

SHORT ANSWER FOR AN INTERNATIONAL APPLICANT: this degree is close to free. Non-EU citizens are TOTALLY EXEMPT from the tuition contribution and pay only the regional right-to-study tax plus a EUR 16 stamp; EU non-Italian citizens pay a flat EUR 200 contribution plus the regional tax and stamp. Realistic 2026/27 totals with a household resident abroad: about EUR 167/year for a non-EU student and about EUR 367/year for an EU non-Italian student. 

THE BINDING RULES (Guida all'iscrizione 2026-27, section 'Esoneri parziali'): 
- 'e. stranieri (cittadinanza in Paesi extra UE): sono esonerati totalmente dal pagamento del contributo di iscrizione; devono versare solo la tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio secondo le disposizioni di cui al punto 1 sopra e l'imposta di bollo, entro il termine ordinario di scadenza per il versamento della I rata.' 
- 'f. europei (cittadinanza in altri Paesi UE): sono tenuti solo al versamento di un contributo fisso pari a 200 EUR per l'iscrizione, se l'importo del contributo dovuto sia pari o superiore a 200 EUR. Se inferiore, possono effettuare l'iscrizione nella modalita ordinaria.' 
- Foreign holders of an annual Italian Government scholarship under development-cooperation or intergovernmental cultural/scientific agreements are also totally exempt from the contribution. 
For ITALIAN students the ISEEU system applies instead: first-year students are exempt up to ISEEU EUR 30,000; above that a fixed component of EUR 1,011.50 plus a variable component, to a maximum of EUR 2,384.00 for those filing no ISEEU declaration. 

REGIONAL RIGHT-TO-STUDY TAX BANDS 2026/27 (D.M. no. 176 of 24 February 2026), three bands: EUR 130.00 for ISEEU up to 25,500.00 and for students from particularly poor countries under art. 13 c. 5 DPCM 9 April 2001; EUR 151.00 for ISEEU between 25,500.01 and 51,000.00 AND for 'studenti con nucleo familiare residente all'estero' (students whose household resides abroad); EUR 173.00 for ISEEU above 51,000.00 or no ISEEU declaration. Stamp duty EUR 16.00. BUDGET EUR 151 IF YOUR FAMILY LIVES ABROAD - that is the band the Guida assigns explicitly to internationally resident households. 

INSTALMENTS: 1st (60% of the contribution + regional tax + stamp) from 16 July 2026 and by 2026-11-02; 2nd (20%) by 2027-03-01; 3rd (20%) by 2027-04-30. Late-enrolment surcharges EUR 50 (to 2027-01-15) and EUR 110 (from 2027-01-16); a further EUR 100 from 2027-07-16 for unpaid 2nd/3rd instalments. Amounts are refundable only where an exemption applies; nothing is refunded on withdrawal from studies. 

[uncertain] TWO DIFFERENT REGIONAL-TAX FIGURES ARE PUBLISHED ON UNINA.IT AND THEY DO NOT AGREE. international.unina.it states 'European students EUR 200/year (tuition fees) + EUR 140/year regional tax (compulsory) + EUR 16.00 legal stamp (compulsory) - Non-european students EUR 140/year regional fee (compulsory) + EUR 16.00 legal stamp (compulsory)', i.e. a flat EUR 140, whereas the binding 2026/27 Guida gives the banded EUR 130 / 151 / 173. USE THE GUIDA; the EUR 140 figure on the international pages looks like a stale carry-over. The tuition components themselves (EUR 200 for EU citizens, total exemption for non-EU citizens) are consistent across both sources. 

NOT APPLICABLE TO THIS DEGREE: the Guida's 40% under-represented-gender discount (ISEE up to EUR 34,000) applies to eight named programmes, and the mechanical one on that list is the BACHELOR 'L in INGEGNERIA MECCANICA: FEMMINILE', not this master's. 
FUNDING: no programme-specific scholarship is published. Regional right-to-study grants come from A.Di.S.U.R.C. (offices at via De Gasperi 45, Napoli), referenced in the department's FAQ index.

1. DIPLOMA NAME vs CURRICULUM NAME - THE CENTRAL POINT OF THIS RECORD. The qualification awarded is the Italian degree 'Ingegneria Meccanica per la Progettazione e la Produzione' (class LM-33). 'Mechanical Engineering for Design and Manufacturing' is the University's official English rendering of that same degree (Didactic Regulations cover; International course catalogue), and 'Sustainable Development' is a curriculum inside it, not a degree title. [uncertain] I found NO unina.it text stating whether the curriculum name is printed on the diploma or on the Diploma Supplement. Italian practice is normally that the curriculum appears on the Diploma Supplement and the transcript, not on the diploma parchment, but that is inference, not a sourced fact for this programme. Anyone relying on the English-language identity of this qualification abroad should assume the certificate reads the Italian degree name. 

2. CORRECTION TO THE RESEARCH BRIEF - THE PROGRAMME HAS THREE CURRICULA, NOT FIVE. The brief says 'Of the programme's 5 curricula, only the Sustainable Development curriculum is taught in English.' The 2026/2027 official sources say three curricula: a Generalist curriculum (itself subdivided into FIVE tracks), a Railway Mechanics curriculum, and the Sustainable Development curriculum. The 'five' in the brief is the number of tracks in the generalist curriculum. The substantive claim in the brief is nonetheless correct: exactly one curriculum, Sustainable Development, is taught in English, and the rest are in Italian. 

3. ENGLISH NAME INCONSISTENCY WITHIN UNINA.IT. The same department uses 'Mechanical Engineering for Design and Manufacturing' (Didactic Regulations, General Information page, brochure, contacts page, International course catalogue) and 'Mechanical Engineering for Design and Production' (site navigation, orientation page, access-requirements text). Track names also vary: 'Advanced and Smart Production' vs 'Advanced and Smart Manufacturing'; 'Road Vehicle Design' vs 'Vehicle Design'; 'Technological Processes' vs 'Manufacturing Processes'. Same programme in all cases. 

4. THE ITALIAN B2 QUESTION FOR NON-EU APPLICANTS IS GENUINELY UNRESOLVED, AND IT IS THE BIGGEST PRACTICAL RISK IN THIS RECORD. The University waives Italian B2 for courses 'in ENGLISH' but registers this degree as ITA/ENG, and Universitaly pre-enrolment is filed against the DEGREE, which has no curriculum field. The waiver sentence on international.unina.it also lists 'three-year, five-year or single-cycle' and omits the two-year magistrale, while the sentence imposing Italian B2 explicitly names 'magistral degree course'. Get this confirmed in writing by the coordinator before filing on Universitaly. 

5. NO PUBLISHED INTERNATIONAL-ADMISSIONS PROCEDURE FOR THIS DEGREE. The department publishes a full international FAQ (documents, Google Form, evaluation, Letter of Acceptance) only for the SISTER degree, Mechanical Engineering for Energy and Environment (LM-IMEA), whose English curriculum is 'Sustainable Energy'. Nothing equivalent exists for LM-IMPP. Everything in required_documents item (4) about a Letter of Acceptance and an English B2/MOI requirement is LM-IMEA practice, cited as a realistic preview, not as a rule for this degree. 

6. AN INTERNAL CONTRADICTION ABOUT ADMISSION LETTERS. international.unina.it states flatly 'The University of Naples Federico II does not issue admission letters for obtaining a visa', while the department's LM-IMEA FAQ describes issuing a Letter of Acceptance uploaded to Universitaly by the Student Office. Both are unina.it pages. For LM-IMPP nothing is published either way. 

7. FEE FIGURES CONFLICT ON UNINA.IT: the binding Guida all'iscrizione 2026-27 gives banded regional taxes of EUR 130 / 151 / 173 (D.M. 176 of 24 February 2026), while international.unina.it still shows a flat EUR 140. Use the Guida. The tuition components (EUR 200 for EU citizens, total exemption for non-EU citizens) agree across both. 

8. SSD LIST DRIFT. The Didactic Regulations 2026-2027 list of acceptable sectors includes IIND-01/F (Fluid dynamics), IIND-01/G (Aerospace propulsion) and PHYS-04/A (Theoretical physics of matter), which do not appear in the department orientation page's rendering; the orientation page in turn labels CHEM-04/A as 'ex CHIM/05 - INDUSTRIAL CHEMISTRY' while the Regulations call it 'Science and Technology of Polymeric Materials'. The Regulations are the newer and controlling text. Also note the department's access statement is anchored to a Teaching Coordination Committee resolution of 23 JULY 2024, i.e. it predates the 2026-2027 Regulations. 

9. NO PUBLISHED FOREIGN-GRADE CONVERSION for the M >= 24/30 personal-preparation threshold, and no published turnaround time for the CCD's evaluation of a foreign transcript. Both are decided case by case. 

10. PER-COURSE LANGUAGE NOT VERIFIED. The English-medium claim for the Sustainable Development curriculum rests on the Didactic Regulations, the Programme Catalogue and the orientamento profile, all of which state it for the curriculum as a whole. I did not find course-sheet-level language fields on unina.it confirming each individual course. Note that several Sustainable Development courses have Italian twins in the generalist tracks (e.g. 'Advanced and Resource Efficient Manufacturing' = 'Tecnologie Speciali'), so course titles alone are not proof of delivery language.

The University's course-catalogue portal is an Angular single-page application that returns only an HTML shell to non-JavaScript clients and exposes no public JSON endpoint that could be located; several probe URLs returned the SPA shell. The course code D19 is nonetheless firmly established from the programme's own contacts page and from an existing course-sheet URL of the form corsi.unina.it/D19/insegnamenti/... .
